title: Level one weight and noise stability
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $0<\rho\le 1$. Write $\widehat f(S)$ for the uniform average of $f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$, and let $W_1(f)=\sum_{|S|=1}\widehat f(S)^2$. If $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(f)$ is the expected product $f(X)f(Y)$ when $X$ is uniform on the Boolean cube and, independently in each coordinate, $Y_i=X_i$ with probability $(1+\rho)/2$ and $Y_i=-X_i$ otherwise, then $\rho W_1(f)\le \operatorname{Stab}_\rho(f)-(\mathbb E f)^2$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube
